title: SEO content brief

sections.title: Reader and goal
fields: Reader
Who is this for? One sentence, specific enough to picture.
Goal
What should they know or be able to do when they finish?

sections.title: Search
fields: Main keyword
The phrase your reader types into Google. Note how many people search it each month.
Related searches
Two or three other phrases or questions people search (from "People also ask" and autocomplete).
What searchers want
Search the keyword yourself. What kind of page shows up most: a how-to, a list, a review?

sections.title: Your angle
fields: What's missing
What none of the top three results do. Fill in page 2 first, then sum it up here.
What only you can add
A story, photo, result, or example from your own experience.
Your angle
The one idea your post adds, in one sentence.
Length
Average the top three, then divide by 3. It's a starting point, not a rule.

sections.title: Next step and proof
fields: Next step for the reader
The one thing they should do after reading (your call to action). Decide it now.
How you'll know it worked
One number to check 30 days after publishing, like your Google ranking or clicks.

ready: You should be able to say the reader, the goal, and what's missing in one sentence each. If you can't, keep researching before you draft.

ranks.title: What already shows up on Google
ranks.hint: Open the top three results that aren't ads. Skim their headings and look for what's missing.
ai: What it covers, and what it leaves out.

outline.title: Outline
outline.hint: Turn the questions people search into your headings. Big questions become sections; follow-up questions become subsections.

sources.title: Sources, photos, and links
sources.hint: Open every source and make sure it still says what you need before you write.

publish.title: Before you publish
items: Main keyword in the title, the first paragraph, and one section heading
Every number links to a source you opened
Two or three links to your other posts
Photos credited, each with a short description for screen readers (alt text)
The next step matches the goal on page 1
A reminder on your calendar to check your number in 30 days

example.title: Example: a filled-in brief
example.subtitle: The brief behind “Owala vs. Stanley: New Colors or New Products?” on angelphommachan.com. Search numbers from Ahrefs, US.
rows: Reader
People starting out in marketing who want to see how two brands grow after one hit product
Goal
Understand the tradeoff between refreshing a best-seller and launching new products
Main keyword
owala vs stanley (1,800 searches a month, easy to rank for)
Related searches
owala color drop (4,600), why is owala so popular (250), stanley marketing strategy
What searchers want
Shoppers comparing the bottles: every top result is a product test
What's missing
No one compared the two brands’ marketing
What only I can add
My own side-by-side read of their products, ads, and blogs
Angle
New colors or new products: what each strategy costs and when it works
Length
Average ÷ 3 ≈ 470 words; finished at about 1,480 to cover products, ads, and blogs
Sources
Retail Dive, Fast Company, The Drum, Owala’s Color Drop FAQ, ASI (each opened and checked)
Next step for the reader
Notice where each brand’s ads and links send you, then answer: refresh it or build something new?
How I’ll know it worked
Google ranking for “owala vs stanley” and time on page after 30 days
note: One quote I planned to use was no longer on Owala’s site, so it came out before drafting. A classmate pointed out that the main growth number came from a search tool companies use to order branded gifts, so the post now says that plainly.
